claim: Kuhn's cycle says anomalies are normal and ignored at first; crisis comes only when failures pile up and resist the frame. Kuhn gives no numeric threshold.
agent_test: Compare reframe-on-first-failure vs reframe-after-N-failed-checks at equal tokens on ARC and multi-step tasks; sweep N=1,2,3,5.

claim: People respond to anomalous data in several ways short of theory change (ignore, reject, exclude, hold, reinterpret, peripheral change); the cause they attribute decides what they do. Chinn and Brewer taxonomy itself was not opened.
agent_test: Log which response type the agent shows when a check fails; test a prompt that forces naming a cause before choosing keep/discard/recollect.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (no external signal) does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0 after two. Gains appear only with oracle labels (GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 -> 59.0). Update 2025: for reasoning-trained models the picture differs (see K27); the Huang result holds for prompted non-reasoning models (Kamoi survey, Self-Contrast).
agent_test: Run the reframe step with and without an external check (test, tool, retrieval) at equal tokens; expect gain only with the check.

claim: A revise or reframe step should be triggered by an external or measured failure signal, not by the model's own sense of doubt.
agent_test: Trigger arms: model-judged doubt vs failed-test count vs consecutive non-improving iterations; same budget.

claim: Reflexion-style retry after an external failure signal improves results. The paper's own text gives +22% AlfWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval and HumanEval 91% vs GPT-4 80%. The reflection step itself adds beyond plain retry (HotPotQA +8% over episodic memory; HumanEval-Rust 0.68 vs 0.60), but only when unit tests supply the failure signal (0.52 without tests). Amended 2026-11-10 after reading the full paper.
agent_test: Store a short verbal lesson after a failed check and retry; compare to plain retry at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs lose accuracy when a familiar rule system is changed (counterfactual tasks) even if the reasoning procedure is unchanged: a sign of recitation of the default frame.
agent_test: Counterfactual restatement of the task as a probe: if accuracy drops on the altered frame, flag stored-frame dependency.

claim: Models cling to stored beliefs when evidence is mixed: ChatGPT keeps its memory answer 3.7% when no evidence supports it vs 99.8% when all does (PopQA); GPT-4 reaches 80% memorisation on popular questions; evidence order shifts results by more than 5 points.
agent_test: Present contradicting evidence in different orders; measure order sensitivity and frame stickiness on popular vs rare facts.

claim: Belief revision is hard for LLMs: in Belief-R the best models sit near 50% combined score (GPT-4-Turbo BU 19.65, BM 82.69, BREU 51.17); chain of thought adds little; good updaters fail to maintain correct beliefs.
agent_test: Test a frame-switch step on Belief-R style items; track both update and maintain accuracy so the step is not a flip-everything bias.

claim: Refutation text (name the misconception, refute it, give the right account) gives a moderate human learning gain: g=0.41 (44 comparisons, n=3,869), about 0.28 after trim-and-fill; older review found no help for grade 11+.
agent_test: Reframe prompt that names the old frame, states why it fails, then gives the new one, vs plain 'try another approach', at equal tokens.

claim: Old information stays active after updating; illustrations and causal explanations did not remove it. Revision is competition for activation, not deletion. Human boundary conditions: persistence after correction is large in a meta-analysis (d=0.75 to 1.06, 52 samples, N=6,878) but inconsistent for person impressions (1 of 3 experiments), and standalone corrections did not backfire (N=1,156). No LLM context-window test found.
agent_test: After a reframe, check whether the agent still uses the old frame's claim later; test an explicit 'retired frame' note in working state.

claim: Learners hold old and new conceptions side by side: transition states with two inconsistent theories (34% to 50% of 5-year-olds), and physics training does not remove misconceptions (r=-.267, N=953).
agent_test: Keep two candidate frames alive and score both on the data rather than overwrite; compare with single-frame replace.

claim: Posner et al. conditions (dissatisfaction, intelligible, plausible, fruitful) are a theory model; support here rests on reviews, not opened data.
agent_test: Gate a reframe on a checklist: current frame fails on named data, new frame is statable and consistent, and it yields a next test.

claim: Explanatory coherence (ECHO, constraint satisfaction) models the oxygen versus phlogiston choice as a settling network; it fits history but no LLM test exists in this evidence.
agent_test: Score two frames with a tally of explained vs contradicted evidence items before choosing; compare with free choice.

claim: LLM discovery agents fail at the full cycle of hypothesis, revision and action: best agent 38% easy and 18% challenge completion; humans 66%. Isolated unit tasks are fine, so the failure is chaining and revising.
agent_test: Compare one-shot hypothesis vs propose-test-revise loops on DiscoveryWorld-like tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Generating several abstract hypotheses and testing each as a program beats direct prompting on ARC (17% direct, 23% program, 30% with LLM summaries, 33% with human pick); iterative refinement helps on rule tasks (ACRE 28.0 -> 59.0).
agent_test: Parallel-frames operator: K frames each tested on the examples, vs one frame retried K times.

claim: LLM rule induction is brittle to noisy or anomalous exemplars; accuracy falls at 12.5%, 25% and 50% corruption, and an instruction to expect noise only reduces the drop.
agent_test: Inject one wrong exemplar and measure whether the agent discards it, reframes, or breaks; compare with an outlier-check step.

claim: Bayesian surprise (belief shift before vs after results) matches human surprise (mean rating 0.67 vs 0.11 for asking the LLM) and finds 5-29% more LLM-surprising discoveries; only 67% of surprising findings also surprise experts.
agent_test: Use belief shift (sample answer distribution before and after evidence) as the impasse signal instead of self-reported surprise.

claim: Experiment design and model proposal remain weak in LLMs: BoxingGym's explicit-model tool does not reliably beat the plain LLM; hyperbolic discounting stays poor after experiments.
agent_test: Do not add a model-fitting stage by default; test it only where the plain loop plateaus.

claim: A scaffold with a Kuhn reframing agent did not beat blind sampling: full scaffold 0.8027 vs one-shot best-of-15 0.8463; floor prompt 0.8906 best; 7 of 10 arms fail the nulls. The Kuhn agent was not ablated. Single independent preprint. Checked 2026-11-10: arXiv v2 (3 Nov 2026) is the latest; the repos hold no Kuhn on/off arm; Kuhn trigger is 5 consecutive rejections plus an externally assigned assumption and domain, never swept.
agent_test: Match any reframe operator against best-of-N one-shot draws at equal tokens; keep it only if it beats that null.

claim: Heavy scaffolding costs mostly context, not reasoning (cache re-reads 2.5x counted tokens; explicit reasoning 2.5% of spend).
agent_test: Meter token cost per operator; cap reframe prompts.

claim: Reasoning models show an aha-like rethink signal ('wait') under RL (AIME 15.6% to 77.9%), but reasoning also collapses past a complexity threshold and overthinks easy items.
agent_test: Compare an inserted reconsideration after a failed check vs none at equal tokens; watch for overthinking on easy items.

claim: Lab studies suggest scientists first blame method, then change the model after repeated anomalies; consistent with a counted-failure threshold. Dunbar counts not read. Gap search could not open Chinn and Brewer or Dunbar; no human counts obtained.
agent_test: Order reframe levels: first re-check procedure and data, then change the model or frame.

claim: Kuhn's oxygen case is stretched as history (SEP) and the Gestalt analogy is uncertain; Bruner-Postman figures were from memory and unverified.
agent_test: Treat the oxygen case as narrative support only, not as a number to build on.

claim: Children's conceptual change and scientists' change are not shown to be the same process; evidence is review-level only.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: A plain challenge ('Are you sure?') makes LLMs flip answers: 46% mean flip rate and 17% mean accuracy drop over 67,640 runs (10 models, 7 tasks). Wrong answers flip more (GPT-4 30.3%) than right ones (10.4%), but right ones still flip. Fine-tuning cuts the drop 60%, not to zero.
agent_test: Run the reframe step on items whose first answer was correct; require correct-to-wrong rate under a set cap at equal tokens.

claim: Untargeted revision overturns correct answers: about 38% of correct answers become wrong after a naive revision step (Snell, MATH); Self-Contrast counts 52 toxic reflections for plain self-reflection vs 11 with contrast of two frames. Selection by verifier or vote, or contrast of two different frames, reduces the loss.
agent_test: Pair every reframe with a select step (vote, test or verifier) that can keep the first answer.

claim: Self-correction blind spot: 14 non-reasoning models show a 64.5% average blind spot (the share of errors they catch when presented as a user's but miss when presented as their own); appending 'Wait' cuts it 89.3%; reasoning models show near-zero blind spot (DeepSeek-V3 0.567 -> 0.902 with Wait vs R1 0.908). So Huang's 'intrinsic self-correction hurts' is conditional on model type and error type.
agent_test: Use a 'Wait'-style re-read as the cheap baseline arm against any heavier reframe operator.

claim: Writing why the attempt failed beats a plain retry, given an external failure signal: Reflexion HotPotQA +8% over episodic memory alone; HumanEval-Rust 50 hardest 0.68 full vs 0.60 without self-reflection; contrast of two frames in Self-Contrast gives 84.4% vs 81.8% for best-of-5 on a GSM8K subset.
agent_test: Arms: plain retry vs explain-failure vs named-old-frame refutation, all with the same failed-test signal and token cap.

claim: Counted triggers are used in practice but never swept: Reflexion reflects after the same action and response repeat more than 3 cycles or after 30 actions and stops after 3 consecutive failures; Smith's Kuhn agent fires after 5 consecutive rejections. No study varies N.
agent_test: Sweep N=1,2,3,5 at equal tokens against best-of-N draws (gap 1 remains open).

claim: Sequential revision vs parallel sampling at equal budget: Snell finds sequential narrowly better with a verifier or vote and a difficulty-dependent best mix (easy: sequential; hard: balance), while Smith 2026 finds a heavy loop loses to blind sampling. The two agree if selection among draws is what pays.
agent_test: Route by difficulty: cheap parallel draws first, reframe only on items that stay unsolved.

claim: An explicit frame-restatement step is unmeasured. Wu et al. show GPT-4 passes the counterfactual comprehension check yet still fails the counterfactual task, so knowing the new frame in a probe does not make the model apply it. Rephrase-and-Respond restates the question only (abstract read).
agent_test: Test restate-then-solve vs solve on counterfactual arithmetic and spatial tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Bayesian surprise needs sampled belief elicitation before and after evidence plus the experiment; boolean elicitation overestimated beliefs and was replaced by five categories. Cost example: 100 experiments about 8 hours with o4-mini. No comparison with a failed-test signal exists.
agent_test: Compare surprise (2 x k samples) with a single failed check and with self-consistency disagreement on single-answer tasks.

claim: No LLM test of an ECHO-style explanatory-coherence tally and no LLM test of a retracted claim persisting in context was found in this gap search (search tools were rate limited, so absence is unproven).
agent_test: Build both tests in our harness: rival-frame coherence scoring and correction-in-context leakage.
